description:
## Problem
`make pr-preflight` runs the tests mapped to the changed files with `uv run -- python -m pytest -q -n 0 ...` (make/pr-landing.mk, the `$$RECORD --name pytest` line). `_should_acquire_test_lock` in tests/conftest.py returns false when `numprocesses` is 0, so this step never takes `~/.benchbox/test.lock`, and it is not wrapped in `host_lock run` either (only the Linux leaf, scripts/linux_preflight_pytest.sh, is). docs/agent/heavy-work.md tells agents to run `make pr-preflight` directly because "its heavy leaf steps already take the lock themselves", and refuses any wrapper. So agents are told not to lock it, and it does not lock itself. Several sessions' preflights then run at once with no admission check or watchdog.

## Evidence
- 2026-11-17 12:34 local: kernel panic on the shared 16 GiB development host, `watchdog timeout: no checkins from watchdogd in 91 seconds` (/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/panic-full-2026-11-17-123444.0002.panic). It followed memory exhaustion while several unlocked `pytest -n 0` preflight runs from different sessions ran together with non-BenchBox load (two omp ablation-eval drivers). A preflight's mapped list can be hundreds of tests (683 on 2026-11-17 for a test_remote_closeout.py change).
- Related but separate: agent-test-policy-documentation (direct `pytest -n 0` by agents), pr-preflight-workflow-selection-cost-20261101 (how many tests preflight maps), heavy-run-admitted-then-killed-by-foreign-memory-pressure-20261112 (admission and kill policy).

## Decision gate (owner)
The 2026-11-17 owner decision on test-lock-refusal-message-advertises-bypass-and-kill-20261117 kept `-n 0` lock-free in general because tooling relies on it. This item asks a narrower question, about the preflight step only. Choose and record in context:
(a) Run the mapped pytest step under `python -m benchbox.utils.host_lock run --admit --guard` (as the Linux leaf does), keeping `-n 0` for the test process itself.
(b) Keep it unlocked and correct docs/agent/heavy-work.md to say so, accepting concurrent preflights.
(c) Another bound, for example a separate preflight-only lock or slot count, chosen with its cost.
Agents must not choose for the owner. Measure the added wait under the current queue (make heavy-status) before the owner decides, if asked.

## Guardrails
- Never set BENCHBOX_SKIP_TEST_LOCK, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ADMIT=force or BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=off; never move or recreate the lock file; never signal another session's process.
- Keep the existing wrapper refusal (a wrapped `make pr-preflight` exits 2) and the nested-holder refusal; the lock must be taken by the leaf, not by a wrapper, so it is never held twice.
- The preflight receipt must still record the step's real exit code; a lock refusal or watchdog stop must be reported as such, not as a test failure or a pass.
- Tests are deterministic and full-suite safe: no real lock contention, no sleeps on wall clocks.

## Verification rubric
Pass only if: the owner's choice is recorded before code changes; under (a) a test shows the pytest leaf runs inside a lock holder and a held lock makes it wait or refuse with the heavy-work exit codes, while the receipt records the outcome; docs/agent/heavy-work.md, docs/internal/dev-loop-worktrees.md ('Test lock') and tests/README.md describe the behaviour that the code has; under (b) the docs no longer claim the step locks. Fail if any new bypass exists or if a lock refusal can produce a passing receipt.
